findings.summary: mutate() calls fn(stateFor(lift)) which still reads the stale outer `sets` closure instead of the updater's `s` parameter, so the race it claims to fix is not actually fixed.
findings.mechanism: stateFor(lift) resolves to `sets[keyFor(lift.id)] ?? seedFor(lift)` using the outer-scope `sets` variable captured at render time, not the `s` passed into the setSets functional updater. Two rapid taps scheduled in the same React batch both close over the same pre-batch `sets`, so the second updater invocation still starts from the same base array as the first and overwrites its change — identical clobbering behavior to before the refactor, despite the code now appearing to be 'inside the updater callback'.
